leads.name: glaze
leads.found_by: toml-lang/toml wiki TOML 1.1 list; Debian source package glaze has no "toml" in its name, so the recorded name search missed it
leads.evidence: Not run. glaze 9.1.0 docs/toml.md: the schema-less TOML targets (glz::generic, glz::generic_i64, glz::generic_u64 and variants) detect only strings, booleans, arrays, floats and integers; the four TOML date-time kinds are read only into typed std::chrono fields of a known schema (local date-times default to UTC), so no documented generic value view can report the four date-time kinds of an unknown document. Its source-package count also covers the JSON-first library, not TOML use.
leads.star_fallback: not eligible: multi-format serialization/reflection/RPC library whose stars reflect JSON and other features (GMarkup rule); also its schema-less TOML targets have no date-time kinds (existing unresolved_api_gap lead)

leads.name: tomlc17 (C++ binding)
leads.found_by: toml-lang/toml wiki TOML 1.1 list ("binding of tomlc17")
leads.evidence: Same tomlc17 family as the C lead; not packaged in Debian, so no primary metric. Not run.
leads.star_fallback: C++ binding src/tomlcpp.hpp (239 lines) over the same src/tomlc17.c selected in the C cell; the documented C++ API (README_CXX.md) reads known keys through get/seek and typed as_* accessors and documents no key enumeration, so a generic walk of an unknown document would read the inherited C toml_datum_t fields, i.e. the C path. Kept as an unresolved_api_gap lead, not a separate C++ path

leads.name: tinytoml
leads.evidence: Not run. README: "This parser is based on TOML v0.4.0". include/toml/toml.h at v0.4 has a single TIME_TYPE holding std::chrono::system_clock::time_point, so the four TOML 1.0.0 date-time kinds of the controls cannot be reported with their exact types; TOML 0.4.0 also lacks the hexadecimal, octal and binary integers and dotted keys of the second control. Not in Debian; 177 stars would meet the star threshold, but the API cannot give the exact typed tree.
